paragraphs: Rabbi Yonatan ben Asmai. (In [Ein Yaakov](https://www.sefaria.org/Ein_Yaakov_(Glick_Edition)%2C_Moed_Katan.1.5): ben Akhmai; in Dikdukei Soferim: ben Chakhmai; and Hyman gives ben Akhmai for [Tanchuma, Bereshit 13](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma%2C_Bereshit.13.2).) He was a disciple of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai, as in [Moed Katan 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.9a.20-23): Rabbi Yonatan ben Asmi and Rabbi Yehuda ben Gerim studied the section on vows in the house of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai. [They] said to him (א״ל), 'Our master, you have taught us.' Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said to his son, 'These people are men of stature; go to them that they may bless you.'[^1]

And he went to them and [they blessed him](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.9b.4-5): 'May it be His will that you sow and not reap, that you bring in and not take out, that your house be laid waste and your lodging be settled, that your table be thrown into confusion, and that you not see a new year.' When he came to his father, he said to him, 'Not only did they not bless us, they even caused us distress!' And he related their words to him, and his father explained to him that they were all great blessings.[^2]

And in [Yevamot 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.15b.7) we find that there was a great family in Jerusalem, of the house of Akhmai. Hyman criticizes [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1881&lang=en) for mixing all three together and wondering at this without recognizing that one was a disciple of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai and he is ben Asmai, and one a colleague of Rabbi Chanina and he is ben Akhinai, and one a disciple of Rabbi Yochanan and he is ben Akhmai.

notes.text: The linked Ein Yaakov reads ben Akhmai. The consulted Tanchuma spells the name ben Akhsai. Hyman reports ben Akhmai for Tanchuma and ben Chakhmai for Dikdukei Soferim.

The Bavli’s blessing scene includes an additional “may you go out and not come in” blessing and explains the seemingly adverse wishes. In Yevamot the family is Beit Tzevoim, described as coming from Ben Akhmai. Hyman and Heilprin call it the house of Akhmai.
